events.region: Southern Trinity; Northeastern Trinity
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 8 and
12 inches possible above 4000 ft, with 3 to 5 inches possible down
to 3500 ft.  Winds gusting as high as 55 mph.

* WHERE...Northeastern Trinity and Southern Trinity. This includes
the higher passes on Highway 3 and 36.

* WHEN...From 7 PM Tuesday to 1 AM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. Tire chains
may be necessary if travelling through mountain passes. Roads, and
especially bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and
hazardous.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Western Garrett; Eastern Garrett; Western Grant; Western Pendleton
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
With high pressure building over the region, temperatures will
cool to near to below freezing across many locations. As winds
turn light and skies remain clear, some patchy fog is expected to
develop, particularly around mountain and river valleys. As
temperatures are likely to be near freezing overnight, some of
this may turn into freezing fog. This may even become locally
dense in spots.

If traveling overnight, please ensure to leave plenty of distance
from the vehicle in front of you. Some slick spots are possible
which may lead to unexpected travel issues.
